analysis.title: Global Markets Daily: Macro Assets in Fed Hiking Cycles
key_insights: GS reviews asset performance around the first Fed hike across nine tightening cycles since 1983. The Fed began a new hiking cycle in September 2026, its first hike since March 2022.

Equities tend to struggle initially after the first hike but recover quickly. In the median of both modest and larger cycles they trough within 2 months and recover within 4 months. 6m returns were flat to positive in all cycles except 1994 and 2022, and 12m returns were positive in all except 2022.
Yields tend to rise into the first hike. After the hike, yields peak locally in modest cycles but keep rising in larger cycles.

The 10y-2y curve tends to flatten into the first hike and keep flattening afterward, more clearly and for longer in larger cycles. GS rates strategists note flattening tends to stop after front-end forward yields peak, when the curve rallies in parallel.
The real trade-weighted USD tends to strengthen into the first hike, with mixed performance afterward.
The market prices roughly three additional hikes, about 100bps of total tightening. GS economists expect one additional hike.
The three smallest cycles (1997, 1999, 2015) are bucketed as 'modest'. 1997 and 2015 were one-hike cycles in which Treasury yields peaked around the hike and then fell.

1997 was strongly positive for risk assets. Inflation was more benign than expected and growth stayed strong, so the market saw dovish policy shocks and positive growth shocks. The Asian Financial Crisis later entered the Fed's thinking.
2015 was less friendly. Growth worries (falling oil, China slowdown, Brexit vote) left equities rangebound and slow to recover to pre-hike levels. The Fed did not hike again until end-2016.

In 1999 the Fed hiked into an investment boom with strong growth and high equity valuations. Yields kept rising, the S&P 500 stayed rangebound, and the tech bubble later burst, contributing to the 2001 recession.

Versus the three modest cycles, 2026 has a strong labor market and a high starting funds rate (closer to 1997 and 1999), growth more like 2015, equity valuations like 1999, and higher starting core inflation than any of them.
GS baseline is a modest number of hikes, growth near potential and gradual inflation relief, implying a modestly positive path for equities.
Risk scenario 1: an earlier end to hiking on better inflation news (likely requiring oil price relief) would be the most positive for risk assets, a mild version of 1997.
Risk scenario 2: an interruption driven by growth worries, most likely if current pockets of financial stress broaden, would be less friendly initially with possible relief later, as in 2015.
Risk scenario 3: if growth holds up, this could be a more extended tightening driven by an investment boom as in 1999, raising the risk of a larger growth downgrade later.
The report lists 18 open trade ideas, mostly FX, EM rates and relative-value equity baskets.

risk_factors: An interruption of hiking driven by growth worries or broadening financial stress would be less friendly for risk assets initially.
A more extended tightening driven by an investment boom raises the risk of a larger growth downgrade later.
Historical analogues have limits: the sample is small and the mix of macro shocks rarely repeats.
Starting core inflation (3.0%) and equity valuations (Shiller P/E 41) are high relative to the modest-cycle analogues.

tension_points.bull_case: A modest number of hikes, growth near potential and gradual inflation relief point to a modestly positive equity path. An earlier end to hikes on inflation relief would be the most positive, like 1997.
tension_points.bear_case: Growth worries or broadening financial stress could interrupt the cycle, which is less friendly initially as in 2015. A longer cycle driven by an investment boom, as in 1999, risks a larger growth downgrade later.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Pockets of financial stress broadening into a wider issue, or growth continuing to hold up so that hikes extend.

theme_stances.key_argument: Baseline of few hikes, stable growth and gradual inflation relief implies a modestly positive path for equities.
